target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): keep blank credentials from overriding AWS auth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Amazon Bedrock users could lose access to the AWS default credential chain when `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, or `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` was present but contained only whitespace. The AWS SDK accepts whitespace values in both its static environment credential provider and its Bedrock bearer-token environment provider, preventing fallback to profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock now trims explicitly configured bearer tokens before selecting bearer authentication. A shared credential-preparation path removes only whitespace bearer/static/session environment values before shared-config refresh and credential resolution; streaming, discovery, embeddings, and control-plane profile resolution all pass through that path. Valid static credentials remain unchanged.

The AWS SDK `fromEnv()` provider checks static values for truthiness rather than trimmed content, while `fromEnvSigningName({ signingName: "bedrock" })` accepts any present `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` value. Removing blank values lets the SDK continue through its normal default chain.

## User Impact

Users with accidentally blank Bedrock credential environment variables can continue using valid AWS profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials across streaming, model discovery, embeddings, and inference-profile resolution. Valid bearer tokens and static credentials remain supported; explicitly configured bearer tokens are normalized before use.

## Evidence

- Direct production-path reproduction on Linux / Node 24.18.0: before the fix, `streamBedrock` configured the AWS client with `{"token":{"token":"   "},"authSchemePreference":["httpBearerAuth"]}` for a whitespace-only bearer token.
- Direct AWS SDK request capture before network I/O: `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` produced `Authorization: Bearer    ` from that configuration.
- After the fix, the same `streamBedrock` path configured no token provider for whitespace-only input; `"  valid-token  "` produced `{ "token": "valid-token" }`.
- Real AWS SDK default-chain proof used an isolated temporary `[default]` shared credentials file, with no network call or real credentials. Before preparation, the SDK selected both whitespace static env credentials and a whitespace Bedrock bearer env token. After preparation it removed those blank values, rejected the missing bearer env token, and resolved the temporary default profile. Redacted result: `{"beforeSelectedWhitespaceStaticEnv":true,"beforeSelectedWhitespaceBearerEnv":true,"blankEnvRemoved":true,"afterSelectedDefaultProfile":true,"blankBearerRejected":true}`.
- Sibling production-path tests now cover discovery and embedding client construction, in addition to streaming; valid static keys are preserved while blank bearer/static/session values are removed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/aws-credential-refresh.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/embedding-provider.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` — 4 files, 97 tests passed.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for the six PR files.
- `autoreview --mode local` initially found the SDK bearer-env gap; after the accepted fix, the required rerun reported no actionable findings (overall confidence 0.97).

AI-assisted. I reviewed the streaming, discovery, embedding, provider-registration, and inference-profile control-plane paths, plus the exact `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node@3.972.61`, and `@aws-sdk/token-providers` contracts.
